text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's exiled king Simeon II, on a second visit to the country he left in 1946, appealed to all political forces contesting Saturday's elections to unite in a broad coalition to push forward badly needed economic reforms.
-- Bulgaria will receive Russian natural gas over the next 15 years under a bilateral accord signed in Moscow by the two countries' prime ministers. @
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA had finalised its purchase of a 60 percent stake in the Bulgarian soda ash producer Sodi Devnya for $160 million.
-- Bulgaria is likely to face a cooking oil shortage next year as the lack of funds and bad weather have delayed sunflower seed sowing, an Agriculture ministry senior official said.

-- The Privatisation Agency is expected to set a new deadline for bids for a 57 percent stake in state owned chemical fertiliser maker Chimko Vratsa because the agency deemed as unsatisfactory the $68 million offer of South Korea's Daewoo, the agency's executive director Alexander Sabotinov said.
-- Bulgaria's comsumer price inflation acclerated to 2,040.5 percent in March year on year from 1,839 percent in February, National Statistics Institute figures showed.

-- Foreign investors have bought Bulgarian bad debt bonds with a par value of some $100 million and have invested 47 billion levs in government T-bills since the beginning of March attracted by the high yields and the stable lev, a central bank official said.
-- Bulgaria's state owned Bulbank posted 12.4 billion levs net profit for last year and 10 billion levs of the net are expected to be used for a capital rise to 15 billion levs.
-- Bulgaria's private First Investment Bank decided to raise capital to five billion levs from 2.2 billion levs. The bank posted 2.28 billion levs gross profit for last year. @

-- Switzerland's Holderbank is expected to pay $5 million in the next few days under a sell-off contract for 51 percent of Bulgaria's state owned cement producer Beloizvorski Ziment, the Construction ministry said. The total price of the deal is $32 million. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
